text:
Samira: Hey team — customer INC-98123 just reported SSO logins started failing right after they rotated the IdP signing cert. They get a 401 from our assertion consumer endpoint. Error in app logs: "SAML validation failed: signature verification failed (no matching certificate)". Ticket attached: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/INC-98123

Josh: On it. Do we have their metadata? Could be cert not included or keyDescriptor ordering weirdness.

Samira: They uploaded fresh metadata to our dashboard. I pulled it and the <ds:X509Certificate> value matches the new thumbprint. But their ACS in metadata is https://app.customer.example.com/sso/acs while their proxy rewrites to /sso/acs/ (trailing slash). Could be recipient/ACS mismatch.

Victor: Trailing slash will fail if our ACS check is strict. We usually normalize but this tenant has strict recipient checks enabled. Can we check the exact SAMLResponse Recipient and InResponseTo?

Samira: Here's the snippet of the SAMLResponse we captured (sanitized):

```
<saml2:AuthnResponse Recipient="https://app.customer.example.com/sso/acs/" InResponseTo="_abc123">
  <ds:Signature>...</ds:Signature>
</saml2:AuthnResponse>
```

Josh: That confirms it — recipient has trailing slash. Our stored ACS is without slash. Two options: (1) ask customer to update metadata to include the exact ACS with slash; (2) we relax recipient check for this tenant to accept either variant while we investigate. Which do we want?

Ida: Before relaxing checks, let's ensure cert rotation isn't also breaking signature chain. I see in the metadata there's also a <KeyDescriptor use="encryption"> appearing before <KeyDescriptor use="signing">. Our parser picks the first signing key; if ordering got swapped, we may be validating with the wrong key.

Victor: Good catch — some IdPs reorder descriptors during rotation. If the signing key isn't flagged properly, signature verify fails even if cert present. We should validate using the KeyInfo in the Signature rather than metadata order if present.

Samira: Customer says their IdP (Onelogin) did a cert rollover with the old cert still valid for 1 hour overlap. They claim everything worked on their side. We started seeing failures ~T+10min after rotation.

Josh: Could be two simultaneous issues: proxy adds trailing slash + our code picks wrong key descriptor. Quick workaround: enable "accept-acs-aliases" for tenant (accept both slash/no-slash) and fallback to verifying signature using any cert in metadata if signature KeyInfo missing. I'll open an eng runbook change but need approval.

Ida: Also we should instruct customer to re-publish metadata with explicit KeyDescriptor use="signing" first and confirm ACS canonicalization matches. But we need a fix for production so users aren't blocked.

Victor: If we relax signature verification order, make sure we log an audit flag so we can revert once they fix metadata — don't want to weaken security permanently.

Samira: Agreed. Proposed immediate steps:
- Support: tell customer to add ACS variant with trailing slash to metadata or update SP config to accept both. Provide exact example metadata snippet.
- Support -> Eng (Josh): temporarily enable accept-acs-aliases for tenant INC-98123 and allow signature fallback to any cert in metadata for the next 2 hours with heightened logging.
- Eng -> Infra (Victor): check their frontend proxy (nginx) for rewrite rules that might be inserting/removing trailing slash. Confirm if we can canonicalize incoming request path before SAML validation.

Josh: I'll put the temporary flag in feature-ops with an expiry: 2 hours from now. Command I'll run (ops CLI):

```
redwood ops set-tenant-config --tenant INC-98123 --config '{"accept_acs_aliases": true, "saml_signature_fallback": true, "saml_temp_relax_until": "2026-03-15T15:30:00Z"}'
```

Victor: For nginx proxies, look for rules like:

```
location /sso/ {
  proxy_pass http://upstream/; # this can strip/add slash
  proxy_redirect off;
}
```

If proxy_pass has a trailing slash mismatch it can rewrite paths. Ask customer to share their proxy conf or confirm that they don't rewrite /sso/acs -> /sso/acs/.

Ida: Also add to runbook: when cert rotation happens, ensure metadata contains both old and new certs during overlap AND that KeyDescriptor for signing is present/explicit. Add validation check to our onboarding pipeline to warn if signing key not first.

Samira: I drafted the message to customer with repro steps and workaround. Sending now. If they confirm they can re-upload metadata, we'll revert temporary relax.

deploy-bot: canary deploy of saml-relax-fallback succeeded in us-east-1 (build 2026.3.15-09) :white_check_mark:

Josh: Deploy looks good. I'm watch-scaling for 30m. If no regressions, we'll keep flag until they update metadata.

Samira: Customer just replied — they can re-publish metadata in 45 minutes. I'll schedule rollback at T+60m. Closing the ticket after verification.

Victor: Follow-up: add automated pre-check during metadata upload that simulates SAMLResponse recipient + signature verify against current SP settings and warn the uploader if mismatch likely. That should cut down these escalations.

Samira: Added follow-up card in product backlog: PROD-1242. Thanks everyone.

Ida: Saved logs and SAML samples to the incident folder: s3://redwood-support/incidents/INC-98123/

Samira: Closing thread once rollback confirmed. :thumbsup:
